title: Alabama Gets Bad News on SEC Title Game
summary: The Alabama Crimson Tide close their regular season on Saturday against the Auburn Tigers in the Iron Bowl. Before even playing that rivalry clash, though, ‘Bama got some bad news about the SEC Championship Game. A matchup with Georgia was awaiting one SEC team this weekend. It won’t be Alabama. content: TUSCALOOSA, ALABAMA - NOVEMBER 21: Head coach Kalen DeBoer of the Alabama Crimson Tide watches his team during the first half of their game against the Chattanooga Mocs at Bryant-Denny Stadium on November 21, 2026 in Tuscaloosa, Alabama. (Photo by Michael Chang/Getty Images) Getty NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - NOVEMBER 14: Keelon Russell #12 of the Alabama Crimson Tide walks off the field after beating the Vanderbilt Commodores at FirstBank Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Carly Mackler/Getty Images) COLLEGE STATION, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 27: Arch Manning #16 of the Texas Longhorns is tackled by Tyree Adams #71 of the Texas A&M Aggies during the second half at Kyle Field on November 27, 2026 in College Station, Texas. (Photo by Alex Slitz/Getty Images) The Alabama Crimson Tide close their regular season on Saturday against the Auburn Tigers in the Iron Bowl. Before even playing that rivalry clash, though, ‘Bama got some bad news about the SEC Championship Game. A matchup with Georgia was awaiting one SEC team this weekend. It won’t be Alabama. Alabama Gets Bad News Getty NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE – NOVEMBER 14: Keelon Russell #12 of the Alabama Crimson Tide walks off the field after beating the Vanderbilt Commodores at FirstBank Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Carly Mackler/Getty Images) Alabama needed a couple of other results to go its way this weekend. The Crimson Tide needed Texas to lose to Texas A&M and Tennessee to lose to Vanderbilt. Those teams entered the weekend with the same SEC records but holding the tiebreaker over ‘Bama. On Friday night, though, Texas already beat Texas A&M. The Longhorns clinched their spot in the SEC title game, ensured of that position by Ole Miss beating Mississippi State in the Egg Bowl earlier on Friday. Alabama will still want to win Saturday for major College Football Playoff seeding implications. But as far as playing in what looks to be the last-ever SEC title game? That has eluded Alabama’s grasp. How Texas Won Getty COLLEGE STATION, TEXAS – NOVEMBER 27: Arch Manning #16 of the Texas Longhorns is tackled by Tyree Adams #71 of the Texas A&M Aggies during the second half at Kyle Field on November 27, 2026 in College Station, Texas. (Photo by Alex Slitz/Getty Images) It was not the prettiest effort from Texas on Friday night. The No. 3 Longhorns only won 16-6 over the unranked Aggies. But particularly in this case, a win was a win. Arch Manning wasn’t at all sharp. He was 18-for-34 passing for a season-low 143 yards. He also threw a costly interception in the fourth quarter. Manning did throw a touchdown for the Longhorns’ only TD, a three-yard pass to Cam Coleman. Gianni Spetic made three field goals for Texas for the final margin. Texas has previously played Georgia in the SEC title game, a 22-19 overtime loss in 2024. After Alabama’s game on Saturday, the Crimson Tide will simply have to wait for the final CFP bracket to be released. title: It's not always pretty, but Longhorns are 10-2 and headed to SEC title game after beating Aggies
summary: The Texas Longhorns found a way to win once again and turned back Texas A&M's upset bid to reach SEC title game against Georgia.
content: Texas quarterback Arch Manning (16) reacts after the team's 16-6 win over Texas A&M during an NCAA college football game in College Station, Friday, Nov. 27, 2026. (Jason Fochtman/Houston Chronicle) COLLEGE STATION - Who needs style points anyway? The narrative might seem a bit repetitive at this point, but Texas followed the exact same script it has all year long to a T and channeled it into another dramatic if somewhat hard-on-the-eyes win. The plot rarely changes in this spectacular 10-2 year for the third-ranked Longhorns that now includes a 16-6 victory over Texas A&M. Only the final margin seems to vary from week to week. But the storyline hasn't gone off course yet as Texas has run off six consecutive wins and, with a 7-2 conference mark, clinched a spot in the SEC Championship in Atlanta next Saturday for the second time in the program's first three seasons in the league. That ain't the only deja vu because the Longhorns will face familiar nemesis Georgia in that game for the second time, too. That's an opponent that has given Steve Sarkisian and the Longhorns nightmares, beating them up three straight times the last two seasons, including in the 2024 title game in overtime. Yeah some reward. Texas celebrates after their 16-6 win over Texas A&M during an NCAA college football game in College Station, Friday, Nov. 27, 2026. (Jason Fochtman/Houston Chronicle) But Texas had to get past the Aggies first. Never mind that the hosts had an eyesore of a record with only one conference win in eight tries. The Longhorns further blackened their record, whipping their rival for the third straight time since joining the SEC in 2024 and sending them spiraling into the long offseason with a 4-8 mark. And they did it as they have most of their wins this fall. The narrative invariably goes something like this. Game kicks off. Gianni Spetic kicks a field goal. Spetic kicks another field goal. Sarkisian calls a few pass plays. The running game gets stuffed. Hey, G, you got another field goal in you? The team gets penalized for everything short of bad breath. And of course, the defense plays their butts off for the entire 60 minutes. What else is new for a Will Muschamp-coached unit that has now allowed zero touchdowns in their last nine quarters against A&M, Arkansas and LSU . The Aggies played their darnedest, but managed just 234 yards and were held to a couple of field goals, which represented something of a step up in progress for them. Cue the Longhorn band. You know, the musicians dressed out in burnt orange and white who were crammed in the south end stands and serenaded those in maroon with "Lit-tle bro-ther, lit-tle bro-ther, lit-tle bro-ther." Several of the Longhorn players celebrated right along with them. Rasheem Biles, Jelani McDonald, Justin Cryer and Derek Williams Jr. jumped into the stands, perched on the wall and sang "The Eyes of Texas." Oh, the offense shows up for a cameo appearance now and again, Biles and Cryer make a jillion tackles, take a bow or two, McDonald comes up with a turnover - his fifth in three games - and Texas keeps moving up the rankings. All the way to No. 3. It's worked out so far. And did again Friday even though Arch Manning threw for just 143 yards - third fewest in his career - with a punitive interception on the doorstep of the Aggie end zone and no receiver had more than Ryan Wingo's and Cam Coleman's 37 yards. "It wasn't very good," Manning said of the offense. Regardless, the Longhorns have maneuvered their way into striking distance of a first-round bye and three weeks off as one of the top four seeds in the College Football Playoff. With their 5-0 record against Top 25 teams, they even have a chance of hanging onto that status, even if they lose to Georgia. Aesthetics be damned. "We've got another opportunity to show the world why we're the best in the country," McDonald said. Without question, this is a Texas team more mentally tough than a bunch of coal miners and one that frequently finds itself in the darkest of circumstances. Who can forget that the Longhorns dropped back-to-back games against unranked foes Oklahoma and Florida before embarking on this impressive, six-game win streak. Three of those wins have come on the road, but that's nothing new for this team either. Remember, this is a team that has won at Tennessee's Neyland Stadium, LSU's Death Valley and now Kyle Field, which is an unholy triumvirate of resting places for opponents. "These are the games you'll remember," senior center Connor Robertson said. "To beat them three years in a row is a cool feeling." Quite frankly, this represents Texas' comfort zone because it never gets flustered and knows its defense will keep it within range, even without All-American edge rusher Colin Simmons, who sat out his fourth game of the season. "Because we've been in them, I don't think anybody panics. We have a level of comfort that we've been here before," Sarkisian said. "Some stuff didn't go our way. But these guys didn't blink. This game is a little bit of a microcosm of our season." Exactly. And while it wasn't a one-score game, it felt like it most of this chilly evening before 109,570 wedged into Kyle Field, most of whom were hopeful the ugliest offense in the SEC just might conjure up the biggest upset in the 121-game history of this nasty rivalry. After all, Mike Elko's highly respected defense contained Texas and held it to a season-low 242 yards, the fewest since it scraped up 179 in an overtime win over Kentucky last year. That emboldened many of the maroon, but they Aggies in turn were throttled by Muschamp's unit, limited to just 15 plays in Texas territory on night and 234 yards overall. It marked the fifth time this season an opponent has creeped forward that futilely. Texas threatened to blow it open several times but relied mostly on Spetic's field goals of 54, 33 and 42 yards and got into the end zone once on a 3-yard scoring strike from Manning to Coleman to cap an 88-yard drive. The rest of the time, the Longhorn defense held the upper hand. Just like the script calls for. "We weren't perfect," Sarkisian said. "It wasn't clean. But we've got a lot more football left to play." Perhaps with the same storyline but a different ending. Subscribe There’s more to Houston with the Chronicle. Subscribe today for just 25¢. title: Texas' Justin Cryer makes himself right at home in Longhorns' win over rival Aggies
summary: Justin Cryer, the former Brookshire Royal High School star, had a big game in his first time playing in the Texas-Texas A&M rivalry, then the transfer celebrated with the Longhorn Band.
content: Texas linebacker Justin Cryer (28) reacts after sacking Texas A&M quarterback Brady Hart during an NCAA college football game in College Station, Friday, Nov. 27, 2026. (Jason Fochtman/Houston Chronicle) COLLEGE STATION - Justin Cryer knows plenty about the Texas-Texas A&M rivalry from his days growing up in the Katy area, but he didn't get his shot to play in it until his fourth year in college. The man everyone calls "Juice" made sure to get the full experience. The Texas Longhorns ' senior linebacker, who transferred from Florida State in January , took a lap around the grass inside Kyle Field hours before Friday night's game, wearing his coat and tie as well as an icy juice box pendant on the diamond chain around his neck. Then, he represented his team at midfield as one of the Longhorns' six captains. Once the action started, there was Cryer again with a huge momentum-stemming sack. And, before his night was done, Cryer had found a spot on the stadium wall shortly after Texas' 16-6 win over Texas A&M , where he joined the Longhorn Band swinging and swaying to the music as all the maroon began to leak out of Kyle Field. BOHLS: It's not always pretty, but Longhorns get it done "It was dope," Cryer said of his first Aggies-Longhorns game. "Being able to run out there and all the tradition that they have here, it was cool to be a part of, and the best part about it: By the end of the game, everybody was gone except for the people in burnt orange." Cryer, who starred at Brookshire Royal High School, had something to do with that hasty exit. With Texas clinging to a 13-6 lead late in the third quarter, the Longhorns offense elected to stay on the field on a fourth-and-1 from the Aggies' 36. When Michael Terry III got stuffed the line, the 109,570 fans - the most at Kyle Field since 2021 - came to life. However, just three plays later on a third-and-7 for Texas A&M, Cryer looped around the right side of the Aggies offensive line and came screaming around the corner where he found himself in the quarterback's lap before Brady Hart even knew he was there. The sack forced a punt and got the ball back to the Texas offense. "That was a huge sack by Juice Cryer," Texas coach Steve Sarkisian said. JUSTIN CRYER SACKS BRADY HART 🤘 @InsideTexas || https://t.co/7PIa9sf9Mo https://t.co/rbhkkaPSKk - Nash (@NashTalksTexas) November 28, 2026 The sack didn't pay immediate dividends. Arch Manning took the Texas offense down the field, but then threw an interception in the end zone, putting the defense back out on the field. It delivered again, stopping the Aggies on a fourth down on Texas' side of the field, which led to a Longhorns field goal that finally put the game away. "If there's a turnover or a punt or whatever (by the Texas offense), it doesn't matter, we're going to go back out there and make sure we get the ball back for our offense," Cryer said. "I love that mindset of this defense that no matter what situation we find ourselves in, we're going to do everything it takes to get the ball back for our offense." Cryer was a freshman on the Florida State team that went 13-0 in the 2023 regular season, but still was left out of the College Football Playoff. He played a bigger role the next two seasons for Seminoles teams that went a combined 7-17. Transferring to Texas, which will be playing in its second SEC Championship Game since joining the conference three years ago, meant Cryer needed to adjust to higher expectations, especially playing for a defense that is one of the top in the nation while supporting an offense that often doesn't do it any favors. "For someone who just got here in January, you've got to assimilate. You've got to get with the program or don't join at all," Cryer said. "Coach Sark has done a good job of building this identity along with (coordinator Will Muschamp) on defense. It's about how you respond. Not everything's going to go your way. You've got to show up and be at your best when your best is needed. On defense especially, we can't control what the other side of the ball does. All we can control is what we do, so if we have to win 3-0, we're going to win 3-0. It doesn't matter. We have a great mindset on defense. There's no complaining, and that's not common, that's not something that happens everywhere. Every time we set on the field, we're all trying to make a play for our offense." And that's how Cryer, the younger brother of former UH basketball star and current Golden State Warrors guard L.J. Cryer, ended up on the railing inside Kyle Field celebrating a win over his team's biggest rival, even if he's been with the team for just 11 months. "(Fellow linebacker Raheem Biles) is down for whatever and he said he was going up there, so if he was going up there, then I was going, too," Cryer said. "It was a fun atmosphere and the game lived up to the reputation. Glad to be a part of it." Subscribe There’s more to Houston with the Chronicle. Subscribe today for just 25¢. title: What West Virginia coach Rich Rodriguez said after losing to No. 2 Utah
summary: West Virginia’s loss to Utah marks the second consecutive season the Mountaineers won’t be attending a bowl game

He’s a really talented thrower, and he’s a competitive runner, and, I think sometimes maybe he gets a little excited,” Mountaineers head coach Rich Rodriguez said after the game. “He’s got the quality reps in practice, but not game reps. It was his first meaningful game reps all year, so it’s a hard. It’s a hard thing. I’m proud of the way he competed, but we don’t give ourselves a chance the way we’re playing defense. content: Gary McDermott: Man United sign up key coach from rivals to strengthen their academy Manchester United are always looking at ways to improve their academy. Hope for future With Mauricio Pochettino at the helm, there will be hope in the youth ranks that the head coach will begin to give more young players a chance. Talented full-back Yulu Helafu has just signed a new deal, and the youngsters will be hoping to prove themselves in the upcoming Youth Cup fixture versus Burnley on Thursday of the upcoming week. New role United’s staff has undergone a seismic change in recent weeks, with Pochettino bringing in his own staff and, in particular, experts to work on fitness, such as his son Sebastiano, who is now part of the coaching set-up. Spaniard Silvia Tuya is also waiting for a work permit to join up as a strength and conditioning coach and will be the first woman to have a coaching role on the male side of the club. The Red Devils have also made a change to their youth department according to Brentford’s official site . The website reads, “Gary McDermott has left Brentford to take up a role in Manchester United’s Academy.” It continues, “during his two years with the Bees, McDermott oversaw a fourth-place finish in the Under-18s Professional Development League and victory in the Under-17s PDL Shield, before leading the Under-18s into the U18 Premier League following the Academy’s promotion to Category One status.” McDermott has plenty of experience with different youth levels, having worked his way up as head coach of the Under-13s and Under-14s before being appointed Under-18s head coach in May 2025. Brentford Academy director David Rainford said, “on behalf of Brentford Football Club, I’d like to thank Gary for everything he has given to the Academy. His hard work and commitment, first with the younger age groups and then with the Under-18s, have helped a number of our young players take important steps in their development. He has played his part in laying the foundations for our first season as a Category One Academy.” Finally, he commented, “Gary leaves with our very best wishes for his new role at Manchester United.” McDermott also has experience coaching the Under-18s at Forest Green Rovers and spent a decade at Southampton, working across the Under-9s to Under-16s, having started his coaching career at Bristol City. title: Hankook tipped to enter race for F1 tyre supply contract
summary: Pirelli is set to face competition from World Rally Championship tyre supplier as well as Bridgestone when the Formula 1 tender process opens next year
content: Motorsport photo It's another vivid demonstration of Formula 1's ever-growing global reach and popularity that another serious contender has emerged to bid for its exclusive tyre-supply contract. Pirelli took over from Bridgestone as F1's sole tyre supplier in 2011 and for much of its first decade it faced little in the way of concerted challenge when renewal time rolled around. That has changed in recent years. Having walked away from F1 in 2010, citing costs and a "strategic realignment" following the global financial crisis, Bridgestone threw its hat in the ring during the most recent tender process in 2023, and is known to be preparing a pitch for the next one. Now Motorsport.com understands that Hankook, exclusive tyre supplier to the World Rally Championship, is assembling a bid for the tender process which opens next year for the post-2028 F1 era. It was previously an unsuccessful bidder in 2018 for the contract covering 2020-23, which was then extended by a year owing to the pandemic. Pirelli's current contract runs from 2025-28, since the company – along with the FIA and F1 – mutually exercised a one-year extension clause last June. During the last tender process, technical stability during the transition to a new formula this season was regarded as a particularly important. Given the impending changes in 2030, potential bidders will have to assure the FIA they can achieve this. While the FIA assesses tenders based on the bidder's technical capacity, sustainability credentials, and the operational capacity to manage the supply process seamlessly, F1 also has a voice in the final decision on commercial grounds. Pirelli is a conspicuously big spender on trackside signage as well as facilitating VIP perks such as the ‘Hot Laps' programme. Hankook has already played a small role in grand prix weekends as a supplier to the W Series in 2021 and 2022. The South Korean company has been involved in motor racing for over three decades, at various times being exclusive supplier to the DTM, along with regional F3 and F4 series. It supplied Formula E's Gen3-era cars from 2022-26 before Bridgestone took on that contract. Hankook Competition CEO Steven Cho (right), seen here with Hyundai's Andrew Wheatley on Rally Japan, has visited several grands prix to meet F1 stakeholders over the past two seasons Hankook Competition CEO Steven Cho (right), seen here with Hyundai's Andrew Wheatley on Rally Japan, has visited several grands prix to meet F1 stakeholders over the past two seasons It was appointed sole tyre supplier of the World Rally Championship in 2025 and this year it was named by the FIA as a member of the governing body's ‘global partner programme'. Representatives including Hankook Competition CEO Steven Cho have attended several grands prix over the past two seasons, most recently last weekend in Las Vegas, and it's understood the company has already conducted testing of prototype tyres with an F2-based ‘mule car'. Having supplied two major FIA world championships in recent years, along with establishing much closer ties with the governing body, it would make this a much more credible bid than the previous one. Formula E is a strong calling card since its environmental aims call for just two different tyre compounds, both made from sustainable materials. Sustainability was Pirelli's finishing move in the last tender process, since it undertook to introduce Forest Stewardship Council-certified tyres to F1 from 2024 onwards. Although based in South Korea, Hankook has an R&D facility in Hanover, Germany, and a factory in Hungary currently undergoing a €450million expansion in Hungary. Pirelli makes its motorsport products, including the F1 tyres, alongside regular road tyres in its factory in Izmit, Turkey. Any company entering the tender process faces a significant challenge because it will be bidding to arrive in year four of the current technical regulations, so it would have to build a very convincing case that it could at least match the existing product. While Pirelli's tyres have come in for regular criticism over the years, this is in the nature of having exclusivity. The current tyres are expected to deliver on a complex and often contradictory set of requirements: they must be thermally and structurally robust, but with a predictable degradation curve to facilitate the spectacle and strategic variety. Experience of the past 15 years demonstrates how easy it is to overshoot either way. Hankook was Formula E's supplier through the Gen 3 era so, besides single-seater experience, it is accustomed to the kind of trackside signage deals that come with the territory Hankook was Formula E's supplier through the Gen 3 era so, besides single-seater experience, it is accustomed to the kind of trackside signage deals that come with the territory "Pirelli has been an important partner to the FIA F1 world championship for many years, providing a consistently high standard of performance, innovation and safety at the highest level of our sport," said FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem when the contact extension was announced in June. "This extension through to the end of 2028 provides stability for the championship." That, along with the prevalence of Pirelli branding around the tracks, paints a clear picture of what any bidder has to offer: deep pockets, and a guarantee that when their tyres go on, nobody will notice any difference apart from the name on the sidewalls. title: Devine lets lead slip away in season-ending loss to reigning champion Yoakum
summary: Enoch Hall and Brody Lane made big plays to help the Warhorses build a halftime lead, but the experienced Bulldogs reeled off 21 straight points in the third quarter to take control.
content: Enoch Hall is a junior running back/defensive back for Devine. (Courtesy/Devine football) Devine was one half of football away from history. But it wasn't to be as its lead slipped away. The Warhorses surrendered 21 third-quarter points en route to a 35-21 loss to defending state champion Yoakum on Friday night at Heroes Stadium in the third round of the Class 3A Division I playoffs. Devine fell one game short of the state quarterfinals, which the Warhorses last reached in 2011. Before that team, only the 1960 Class 2A state semifinal squad reached those heights in program history. PLAYOFF SCORES: San Antonio high school football third-round playoff scoreboard On Friday, the Warhorses struggled to contain Yoakum junior Elyjai Barnett, who rushed for 102 yards and five touchdowns, four of which came in the second half. "I thought we had him a number of times," Devine coach Jacob Campsey said. "There were a couple fourth downs where we had him bottled up in the backfield, and then we just don't get him down. "They're really good up front. He's a tremendous competitor, and we had him where we wanted him. We just couldn't quite make those plays." Yoakum recovered the opening kickoff after the short kick landed between two Devine players and bounced into Bulldogs senior Brady Elder's hands at the Warhorses' 23-yard line. The special teams blunder gave the Bulldogs a short field. Three carries from sophomore Deion Williams and a facemask penalty on Devine put Yoakum on the 3-yard line, where Barnett scored his first touchdown of the night from the wildcat formation. Devine tied the game midway through the second quarter after sophomore Nathan Valle found junior Enoch Hall streaking open up the right seam for a 29-yard touchdown. WOLVES MOVE ON: Davenport routs Canyon Lake to advance to state quarterfinals "He's just such a gritty competitor," Campsey said of Hall. "On top of the talent, he's a bull rider and he's tough. He's really skilled, such a tough kid. He just gets up and takes hits. I'm so proud of him." After forcing a quick Bulldogs three-and-out, Devine pulled ahead with six seconds remaining in the half when junior Brody Lane motioned into a jet sweep and turned the corner for a 5-yard rushing touchdown. Yoakum coach Bo Robinson said his team hadn't faced adversity in "the last two and a half months." "Devine played really well," Robinson said. "They were probably better than I even thought they were. And I thought they were good on film. "We just came out in the second half and put our nose to the grindstone." BRENNAN ADVANCES: Jeremiah Conwell's late TD pass lifts Bears over Lake Travis The Bulldogs began to pull away when they leaned on Barnett in an intentional simplification of the second-half game plan. "He's just a good player. He's a tough player," Robinson said of Barnett. Early in the third, Barnett ripped off two rushing touchdowns of 30 yards or more as Yoakum promptly took a 21-14 lead with 6:29 remaining in the third quarter. As Valle and the Warhorses' offense struggled to find their rhythm after halftime, Barnett added his fourth touchdown, an 11-yard wildcat score with 31 seconds left in the quarter. Despite watching its lead vanish and falling behind by 14, Devine kept fighting. Valle connected with junior Payten Edwards in the right corner of the endzone for an 18-yard touchdown that cut Devine's deficit to 28-21 with 7:36 left on the clock. RANGERS ROLL: Smithson Valley handles Medina Valley to advance to state quarterfinals "They're just such fighters," Campsey said of his team. "They play the game the right way. And they just give themselves a chance." Barnett's fifth and final touchdown put Yoakum ahead 35-21 with just over two minutes remaining. As the Warhorses kept fighting, they lost their leader. On the ensuing Devine possession, Valle exited the game after suffering an undisclosed injury. Bulldogs sophomore Rae'Sean Samuel picked off Valle's backup, Charles Stricker, to seal the game. While the loss stings, Devine made significant strides in Campsey's first year as head coach. The Warhorses won a playoff game for the first time since 2015 and reached the third round for the first time since that special 2011 team. "These seniors, they raised the bar of this program," Campsey said. "This is where we want to live all the time, late in the playoffs, and they did that. "It's a testament to those guys' belief and commitment." Subscribe There’s more to San Antonio with the Express-News. Subscribe today for just 25¢. title: Merritt Island beats Eau Gallie for first regional title in five years
summary: Merritt Island defeated Eau Gallie 24-21 to win its first regional title in five years while Holy Trinity will play for its first state championship.
content: MERRITT ISLAND — Since the summer, it felt destined that Eau Gallie would play Merritt Island in the Class 3A, Region 2 final. After the Mustangs rallied for a 36-35 overtime win in the regular season, the two sides met again on Nov. 27 for a berth into the state semifinals. It was a back-and-forth game that featured four lead changes, but Merritt Island secured the regional championship on a big game from junior Zaylan Chapple and a timely defensive interception from senior Elijah Floyd in a 24-21 victory. “I’m so proud of the whole team. They fought tooth and nail. They’re a good football team. It was a dang good battle last time we played them,” Merritt Island head coach Tyler Murray said. “It was the same as a heavyweight title fight. They threw a blow, we throw a blow and at the end of the day we came out standing on top of them and they ended it.” Chapple powers Mustangs offense In a battle of two elite running backs, Chapple made his mark carrying the ball 25 times for 174 yards and all three Merritt Island touchdowns. “It’s great, especially my line,” Chapple said. “They got me there and my tight end. They kept pushing and didn’t stop.” After a 39-yard field goal by senior Liam Miller opened the scoring, Chapple extended the Mustangs lead to 10-0 on the first play of the second quarter with a 28-yard touchdown run. The score came off a turnover over on downs by Eau Gallie following a failed fake punt. Chapple put Merritt Island back into the lead in the final minute of the first half on a 5-yard touchdown run to cap a 3:40 drive. The junior scored the eventual winning touchdown on a 2-yard run with 3:43 left in the third quarter. “We watched film and they ran a lot of zone, so if they give me the ball I can get first downs and touchdowns,” Chapple said. Merritt Island was able to ice the game on a 32-yard run by Chapple on 3rd-and-11. The drive was set up on an interception from Floyd for the game’s only takeaway. It was Floyd’s second interception of the season. “Just a total team win. Holding those guys with all those kinds of athletes to 21 points, got to give it up to the defense,” Murray said. “Huge defensive stops when they needed it. Big turnover at the end by Elijah Floyd. Someone’s got to get him late and get a diamond in the rough because that kid’s a baller.” Commodores marred by self-inflicted mistakes It was another frustrating night for Eau Gallie as it couldn’t find the go-ahead score on the final three possessions of the game trailing by three. “We left a lot of plays out there. Our kids played really hard, but obviously they had more points than us at the end,” Eau Gallie head coach Chris Sands said. “Hats off to them and the energy they had the entire game. Their coaching staff should be really proud of their team.” Eau Gallie committed 19 penalties for 171 yards in the regular-season meeting on Oct. 9. The Commodores ended the regional final with 10 penalties for 109 yards. No penalty was more costly than in the third quarter. Miller converted a field goal to trim the Eau Gallie lead to 21-20 only for the drive to be extended on a personal foul penalty by the Commodores. That 15-yarder and automatic first down led to Chapple’s game-winning touchdown. “It was huge. We tried to deal with it. A lot of it I thought effort stuff. We didn’t have many personal fouls or anything like that. A handful of holding calls,” Sands said. “We just got to figure out a way to get better next season and find a way to regroup and make sure we keep moving forward.” In just his second game back from suffering an injury on Sept. 4, Eau Gallie sophomore X’Zavier Corbin produced another huge performance. Corbin rushed the ball 19 times for 212 yards and one touchdown. After returning in the regional semifinals, Corbin concluded the playoffs with over 500 rushing yards. “(Corbin’s) one of a kind. He plays his tail off every time he goes in there. We’re really proud of him they way he responded, especially what they were doing with him,” Sands said. “They were just trying to get him out of his game a little bit and he kind of settled down and made some plays.” Eau Gallie overcame an early 10-0 deficit to take the lead. Commodores senior Joseph Allen connected with junior Zay Hawkins for a 17-yard touchdown completion at the halfway mark of the second quarter. On the next offensive snap, Corbin outran the Mustangs defense with a 66-yard touchdown run. The Commodores reclaimed the lead with 8:32 left in the third quarter on an Allen to Hawkins touchdown connection for 46 yards. Eau Gallie punted twice and Allen threw an interception with 2:50 remaining in regulation. “We got stuck back and had a negative play and ended up at third and long. We just couldn’t get ahead of the sticks most of the night,” Sands said. “It was a lot what they’re doing and obviously we missed some plays out there so it was stuff we were doing as well.” In a season that began with championship aspirations, Eau Gallie’s season comes to an end following an adversity-filled 8-5 season. Four of its five defeats came to regional champions. “I thought out kids really gutted out a lot of wins. Played a really tough schedule and put us to this point to practice on Thanksgiving again and have a chance to go to the final four,” Sands said. “It wasn’t enough. Hats off to Merritt Island and their staff for getting their kids over the hump this year. Hopefully they can win state for Brevard County.” The Commodores graduate 21 seniors. They helped Eau Gallie reach its third-straight regional final, including a regional title in 2024. “Gritty, tough. Obviously, it starts with Joseph Allen, a kid that has done a lot for our program. We’re proud of all of them the way they responded to adversity this season,” Sands said. “They led our group to a great season. We just couldn’t get those last couple plays and I wish we did, but at the end of the day that’s football.” Final four bound Merritt Island marches on to the Class 3A state semifinals. The Mustangs are back in the final four for the first time since 2021. “I’m just so proud of my staff, so proud of the guys, so proud of Mustang nation supporting us,” Murray said. “I’m just so proud to be a Mustang, born and raised, and we’re going to back to the final four. Let’s get it.” The Mustangs will likely host a state semifinal on Dec. 4 as the No. 2 seed. The official state semifinal pairs won’t be announced until the conclusion of the remaining state playoff games taking place on Nov. 28. “It’s been like that all year. We’re a 1-0 team,” Murray said. “That’s what we’ve been preaching since June and we’re going to continue to preach it through the rest of the year.” Independent League Pool B, South Region (1) Holy Trinity 38, (2) Santa Fe Catholic 14 For the first time in school history, Holy Trinity will play for a state championship following a convincing win over Santa Fe Catholic. The Tigers, playing in their first-ever regional final, led wire-to-wire behind three touchdowns from sophomore Jacorey Mills and three touchdown passes from sophomore Jackson Mobley. Mills rushed for touchdowns of 80 and 85 yards. Mobley threw a 94-yard touchdown pass to senior Chandler Hendley, a 64-yard screen touchdown pass to Mills and a 16-yard score to junior Zach Curran. Holy Trinity will compete in the inaugural Independent League Pool B state championship game versus Jay on Dec. 4 at The Villages Charter. title: Penn State rallies to beat Mississippi State in Battle 4 Atlantis

content: The Penn State men's basketball team came through with a big second-half effort to leave the Bahamas with a win in the Battle 4 Atlantis. title: After 14-point quarter against Philly, Pacers should expect more zone
summary: The Pacers have been effective around the rim even as they've missed 3s, but the 76ers zone Friday kept them from doing either in a 111-87 loss.
content: INDIANAPOLIS -- The Pacers' second 3-pointer Friday night was a gift from the 76ers' 2-3 zone defense. On that one possession, the Pacers made the zone move the way they wanted it to and got a clean look for their best outside shooter so far this season, and that knocked it down. Rookie point guard Braden Smith brought the ball down the floor with about 1:27 to go in the second quarter and dribbled over to the right elbow. Center Ivica Zubac found space to post up in the middle of the floor free throw line while All-Star forward Pascal Siakam worked toward the baseline. Zubac caught a pass from Smith to draw 76ers center Joel Embiid up to guard him, head-faked a pass to Siakam cutting to the rim to get LeBron James and 76ers second-year guard V.J. Edgecombe to collapse toward him. That left Pacers guard Andrew Nembhard wide open at the left elbow and Zubac whipped a pass to him for an open 3 while Edgecombe gave a token effort on a closeout but never got close to getting a hand in Nembhard's face. Nembhard -- the only Pacers player with more than two attempts who is shooting better than 40% from 3-point range this season -- swished a 3 and made it look easy. However, the 76ers wisely trusted that the Pacers couldn't pull that off again, or at least couldn't pull it off enough times to consider changing strategy. They were right and they held the Pacers to their worst scoring output of the season in a 111-87 win Friday night in an NBA Cup East Group B game at Gainbridge Fieldhouse and exposed a new vulnerability for a team that has plenty enough already. The Pacers fell to 6-13 overall, 1-3 in East Group B and missed out on a last-gap effort to advance to the knockout round while the 76ers won Group B and earned the East's No. 3 seed in the tournament that will end with its title game on Dec. 11 at Hinkle Fieldhouse. Philadelphia coach Nick Nurse -- a long-time proponent of various forms of zone defense -- switched to mostly zone looks with over eight minutes to go in Friday's second quarter. The Pacers hadn't seen much zone this season, but given the extent to which it short-circuited their offense Friday, more teams should probably try it until Indiana either gets All-Star point guard Tyrese Haliburton back or proves it can consistently hit outside shots. Or perhaps both. Prior to the switch, the Pacers were able to at least keep the game competitive by getting the ball to the rim even while not making 3s. However, the 76ers simply put more bodies around the rim, took the paint points away and were never burned for it. The Pacers scored a season-low 87 points with just 14 in the third quarter, a season-low for any period. They shot a season-worst 34.9% from the floor and made a season-low five 3-pointers on 37 attempts for a season-worst 13.5% from beyond the arc. A frustrated Rick Carlisle didn't want to speak much to the specifics of the offensive meltdown Friday and simply wanted to move on to the second night of a back-to-back coming on Saturday night in Chicago. "Some nights it's like that," Carlisle said. "I don't like the way this game went. I know we can play a lot better. I know we can compete a lot better. But it happened and it's over and now we've gotta turn toward tomorrow." Still, teams that watch video from Friday night are going to see an obvious strategy of attack against a Pacers team that will be digging out of a hole even when it does get its franchise player back and will still have some obvious weaknesses it needs to address. For all of the injury issues they've dealt with, the Pacers have managed to develop an approach with the personnel they have that allows them to get the ball to the rim for layups and dunks. In Nembhard, backup point guard T.J. McConnell, combo guard Quenton Jackson and even rookie Braden Smith they have guards who can attack the paint off the dribble. Zubac gives them a punishing big man who can score in the post, off screen-and-rolls and off of putbacks. Siakam's 7-3 wingspan and remarkably tight handle make him one of the hardest players in the league to keep away from the rim. The Pacers actually rank third in the NBA in points in the paint per game at 51.9 behind only the Pelicans and Spurs. However, 46.7% of their points come in the paint, which puts them second in that category behind New Orleans. So in theory a great way to shut the Pacers' water off is to wall off the paint, and the 76ers did exactly that. It helped, of course, that they had the personnel to do it, starting with 7-foot center Joel Embiid who didn't block any shots but still deterred drives just with his presence. Even at 41, the 6-9 James is still not to be tested at the rim. The 6-9 Dominick Barlow, starting in place of injured All-NBA forward Jaylen Brown, gave them even more rim protection as he recorded a pair of blocked shots to go with 12 points and eight rebounds. The 76ers also had size coming off the benchin center Adem Bona and forward Jabari Walker. "A big player at the rim was contesting," Nembhard said. "In a zone, he can stay in that spot the whole time." The Pacers didn't have too much of a problem going around them and through them when they were in man-to-man. They made 6-of-9 field goal attempts in the paint in the first quarter and 12 of their first 19 overall. After that -- essentially once the 76ers switched to zone -- they made just one of their next 15 paint shots. They were 3 of 14 in the lane in the decisive third quarter when they were also 5 of 25 from the floor and 1 of 8 from 3. They went 9 of 10 in the fourth quarter with the game mostly decided for a respectable 48 paint points for the game, but their shortcomings there were decisive. Several of the players they can usually count on for paint points struggled. Siakam scored 11 points, but he was 3 of 14 from the floor. Zubac grabbed 16 rebounds, but he was 2 of 7 from the field. Free agent wing Kelly Oubre Jr. has been dynamic getting to the rim on cuts and drives in recent games, but he was 1 of 6 from the floor. The Pacers cot some points by drawing contact and made 22 of 32 free throws, but that didn't make up for their lull in the paint. "They have Embiid standing in there and we've gotta go better than 1-for-15," Carlisle said. "It's an easy answer. And we gotta be able to knock in some shots." But of course, they haven't knocked in shots all season, and Friday night was simply the worst night of many in that regard. They made just 1 of 10 first-quarter 3-point attempts and just 2 of 17 by halftime. Nembhard and center Jay Huff combined go make four 3s on 12 attempts. The rest of the team finished 1 of 25 from 3 with Jackson coming through with the only make. "I think tonight specifically, we did a good job of creating shots for ourselves that were pretty good looks," Nembhard said. "They just couldn't fall for us." They haven't all year, which is all the more reason for teams to play zone, pack the paint and present them with open outside looks with no fear that they actually will fall. After Friday, they rank 26th in the 30-team NBA in made 3-pointers per game with 11.4 per game and 29th in 3-point percentage at .322. They've shot better than 40% from 3-point range in just five of their 19 games this season and been held under 30% eight times and under 32% 11 times. In 10 of their 19 games, they've hit 10 or fewer 3-pointers. It obviously hurts that they're missing Haliburton, a career 39.2% 3-point shooter who hit 218 3s in his last full season in 2024-25. He's not only the Pacers' most prolific shooter, but his gravity and elite passing creates better opportunities for others. That said, very capable shooters are missing make-able shots. Forward Aaron Nesmith -- who hit the most 3-pointers of any player who took part in the 2025 postseason -- continued a nightmarish shooting season Friday by missing all four of his 3-pointers and hitting on just 1 of 8 field goal attempts. He's missed 17 straight 3-pointers with his last make coming two weeks ago in the Pacers' Nov. 13 win over the Knicks. He's made just 2 of his last 24 3s and is 20 of 80 (25%) from 3 for the season while also shooting 35.5% from the floor. He's a career 37.7% 3-point shooter including 38.8% in his fifth year as a Pacer and he's twice cracked 41% for a season. Nesmith is having the worst go of it, especially among accomplished shooters, but he's not the only one struggling. Nembhard is the outlier, making 41% of his 3s. He's never shot better than 36.1% from 3 so he's the only one who's made a markable improvement and he's the only player averaging better than two 3s per game. Forward Larry Nance Jr -- shooting 38.5% at 15-of-39 -- is the only other Pacers player who has appeared in more than five games who is shooting better than 36%. Siakam and Smith are both at 35.3%. Jackson and Huff are both around 32%. Forward Obi Toppin is just over 30% and wings Kelly Oubre Jr. and Jarace Walker join Nesmith under 30%. "We're just keeping each other up," Huff said. "Not getting down on yourself. We're all going through it together. And trying to pull up the next man up with you." It's as good of an approach as any to trying to break out of the team's collective slump, but if they don't start knocking down 3s, they'll see more teams willing to devote more bodies in the paint to keeping them from making the shots they actually are making. title: LeBron James’ performance against Pacers led to Jalen Rose sharing a Michael Jordan reminder
summary: Jalen Rose clearly did not appreciate what 41-year-old LeBron James did against the Indiana Pacers in a 111-87 Philadelphia 76ers win. Rose spent six seasons as a Pacer and is considered among the franchise’s cult legends.
content: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images Jalen Rose clearly did not appreciate what 41-year-old LeBron James did against the Indiana Pacers in a 111-87 Philadelphia 76ers win. Rose spent six seasons as a Pacer and is considered among the franchise’s cult legends. As LeBron and the 76ers came to town to defeat the Pacers in a one-sided clash on November 27, Rose decided to bring up Michael Jordan instead of reacting to the 41-year-old in Year 24, who dropped 21 points, seven rebounds and six assists, with a strong defensive showing as well. Jalen Rose reminds fans Michael Jordan is still the NBA GOAT over LeBron James Rose took to his social media to name Jordan as the NBA GOAT while ignoring LeBron’s ongoing performance against his former Pacers at the time. “MJ is the GOAT” Rose also made a similar post about Tupac Shakur being the GOAT in hip-hop, so he might just have been appealing to broader cultural points. But the timing of the Jordan GOAT post, as LeBron was having a great game against a team Rose has a soft spot for, seemed dubious to the fans in his replies as well. There can never be one absolute GOAT in basketball. Even before LeBron emerged, people debated Jordan and Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, with Kareem and Wilt Chamberlain before that. Jordan’s peak accomplishments like two three-peats, a 6-0 NBA Finals record and 10 scoring titles might never be replicated. Fans who put stock in peak performance will always go with Jordan. However, fans who place more importance on the larger body of work one puts together over his career, regardless of the absolute championship result, often support LeBron as the GOAT due to the totality of his accomplishments and his longevity, setting benchmarks previously thought to be impossible. James is averaging 17.4 points, 6.9 rebounds and 6.8 assists with the 76ers this season, the lowest scoring mark of his entire career, but he’s averaging 22.4 points, 6.6 assists and 6.4 rebounds over the last five games, proving he is coming into his peak form now. content: ‘Hard to Watch’ — Ben Roethlisberger Reacts to Mike Tomlin’s ‘Dumpster Fire’ Remarks After Aaron Rodgers-Mike McCarthy Controversy The Aaron Rodgers flameout will go down in the annals of NFL history as one of the most spectacular storylines we’ve ever seen, a turn of events that will bookend the career of a future first-ballot Hall of Famer. With Rodgers well and truly out the building, Mason Rudolph got the start against the Denver Broncos on Black Friday as the Steelers ran riot over the visitors at Acrisure Stadium. While Pittsburgh eventually wrapped up a pretty eventful week with a win, the very public dispute between Rodgers and Mike McCarthy prompted franchise legend Ben Roethlisberger to weigh in on the entire mess. Ben Roethlisberger Reacts to Steelers’ Ugly Aaron Rodgers-Mike McCarthy Drama Roethlisberger established himself as one of the greatest quarterbacks in Steelers history during his nearly two-decade career in Pittsburgh. He led them to two Super Bowl championships following the 2005 and 2008 seasons and made another appearance in the championship game in 2010. Roethlisberger also moved another step closer to a Pro Football Hall of Fame induction after being included among the 52 players under consideration for the Class of 2027 last week. However, he is now watching his former team deal with an unexpected controversy involving Rodgers and McCarthy. “It’s like you have a side, and my side is going to be the Pittsburgh Steelers and Mr. (Art) Rooney and the Rooney family, that logo, that emblem, and the fans,” Roethlisberger said on his podcast. “Because the fans of this team and this organization, not just in this city, but around the world live, breathe, and die for this team.” Mike Tomlin also admitted that the situation upset him as he had personal relationships with both individuals. He said that he had spent time working with Rodgers and developing a relationship with him over the past couple of years, while also having known and competed against McCarthy for a long time. Tomlin also acknowledged that the entire situation had been upsetting for him. “I’m upset about it,” Tomlin said. “It’s a dumpster fire, and I don’t say that in a judgmental way. I presided over a few dumpster fires in my 19 years. But it certainly is upsetting, and I’m sure Steelers nation is upset.” Roethlisberger, for his part, admitted that watching the turmoil had been difficult. “And the Coach Tomlin dumpster fire that has been this week has been hard to watch,” Roethlisberger added. “And I joke that, like ever, the Cleveland Browns have been sitting in Cleveland looking at us, laughing at us because of what we’re going through.” McCarthy could face a challenge rebuilding trust and strengthening relationships following the drama with Rodgers, who ranks No. 29 in PFN QB Impact with a 67.0 grade. But there are indications that he still has support inside the locker room, as Rudolph expressed his backing for the head coach through an Instagram story following Friday’s win. The win over Denver will go some way towards easing tensions inside the building, especially given the fact that the Broncos were on a six-game winning streak before visiting Pittsburgh. The Steelers’ next Aaron Rodgers-less game comes against the Houston Texans in Week 13 on Sunday Night Football. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

title: ‘Shame on you’ – Ben Roethlisberger shares what he’s ‘heard’ about the Rodgers-McCarthy saga
summary: Although the Pittsburgh Steelers answered in style with an emphatic victory over the Denver Broncos on Friday, the Aaron Rodgers saga will just not be going away any time soon. content: Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images Although the Pittsburgh Steelers answered in style with an emphatic victory over the Denver Broncos on Friday, the Aaron Rodgers saga will just not be going away any time soon. Mike McCarthy has endured a week of backlash and accusations following his former quarterback’s fiery interview on The Pat McAfee Show. This could have easily derailed the Steelers for good, considering they had already lost their prior two games. However, it seems to have galvanised the team, and Ben Roethlisberger has now had his say on this week’s events, with the Hall of Fame nominee sharing what he has been told by some inside the Steelers’ building about the veteran head coach. Ben Roethlisberger weighs in on Aaron Rodgers-Mike McCarthy saga Ultimately, what has gone down this week has done no one any favours. Fortunately for the Steelers , they were able to put the debacle to one side and get on with their on-field business ahead of the game against the Broncos, but Roethlisberger has admitted he’s heard the rumours about McCarthy are largely true. “Soap opera, you could call it what you want. I fall somewhere in the middle, where I think like, ‘Shame on this, and shame on this.’ If there is truth, and I’ve heard it from other people, about the McCarthy accusations, the missing meetings, the late to walk-throughs, the not watching film, with those accusations, it’s like, ‘Shame on you Mike,’ depending on how much truth there is to that,” Roethlisberger said on Footbahlin podcast. “To hear some of the stuff, it’s just like, ‘Holy cow, I can’t believe it.’ The Coach [Mike] Tomlin dumpster fire that has been this week, has been hard to watch. That being said, I know the way Aaron went on the McAfee show and aired it all out. I think there’s a lot of people that are like, ‘Hold on now. We don’t air out that locker room stuff like this.'” There will likely be a lot of Steelers fans feeling the same way this week. McCarthy has certainly got his flaws, which this will all hopefully act as a wake-up call – literally – to the 63-year-old to change some of his habits. However, Rodgers has received significant backlash from a lot of former players and media members for breaking the code of the locker room and airing out the team’s dirty laundry. Some will feel as if he did that to wake the Steelers execs up to what was going on, but a lot still believe that Rodgers was only attempting to take McCarthy down with him. Jalen Ramsey’s take on Mike McCarthy has fans questioning Aaron Rodgers. After the Steelers beat the Broncos, Ramsey gave an interview where he emphatically said that the locker room had coach McCarthy’s back, with them responding on the field with the win. “For the past couple of days, we, as players, kind of (did the talking). We were like, ‘Coach, you good’ — let us turn this up. Let us get in our zone.” With the Steelers picking up a win and star CB Ramsey galvanising the team behind their under-fire coach, fans think Rodgers’ departure might have served the franchise well. “This is a really bad look on Aaron,” said one fan after Ramsey’s comments directly undercut Rodgers’ claim of McCarthy losing the locker room. “That’s good. Don’t let the toxic bully win by dividing the team against the coach,” believed another fan . “You pick each other up when the chips are down. McCarthy had a tough week. They could see that. These two are leaders. Obviously McCarthy hasn’t lost the locker room,” said a fan about the coach and the locker room’s response . “I think it was an issue between QB and playcaller/coach. Ramsey also clarified his personal relationship with Rodgers at the time, reiterating that the QB is also their brother and that the pair have spoken since his release. “We’re not going to act like Aaron wasn’t our brother for these past two years.” With the Steelers still in the playoff hunt, this midseason reshuffle might give them the spark they need to secure their position in the AFC North with a 7-4 record, just half a game behind division leaders Cincinnati Bengals. This past Sunday night saw the most anticipated trade in the NHL go down. The Detroit Red Wings traded Dylan Larkin to the Montreal Canadiens in a stunning deal that included four players and six draft picks. It’s a move that will impact each team moving forward in big ways. For the Red Wings, it’s a bit straightforward. They got four draft picks and three players in the deal. Kirby Dach and Samuel Montembeault will contribute as soon as possible in the NHL. Top prospect Michael Hage is waiting in the wings, so to speak, and will likely be a big part of the team next year. All the while, Detroit moves forward with its eye on the future. For the Canadiens, though, the future is in the here and now. Larkin’s acquisition opens Montreal’s Stanley Cup window. The Habs went to the Eastern Conference Finals last year without him on the team. What can a fully motivated Larkin add to the team this year? Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) This also begs a question that applies to both teams. What comes next after this blockbuster trade? The Red Wings’ next move is also straightforward. Montreal’s next move will be difficult, but there is certainly one area on the ice that could use improvement. Canadiens should look for defensive help on trade market David Kirouac-Imagn Images The Canadiens have a very good forward group at this time. Montreal already had Nick Suzuki, Juraj Slafkovsky, and Cole Caufield prior to adding Dylan Larkin. The gold-medal-winning center only boosts an already strong group for the Habs. However, the team could use a bit of help on defense. The Canadiens have star talent in the forms of Lane Hutson and Noah Dobson. But the rest of the group does leave something to be desired. Hutson and Dobson are also not the strongest on the defensive end of the ice, which doesn’t help matters. The good thing for Montreal is that there are legitimate options they can trade for. The trade market is rife with defensemen that could improve the blueline in its own zone. Oliver-Ekman Larsson is a solid defender while also chipping in offense. Zach Whitecloud is an underrated option who would boost the third pair. The Habs could also take a flier on a younger guy such as Kevin Korchinski. The issue for the Canadiens is cost. Not trade cost, mind you, but the financial cost. As things stand, Montreal has a little more than $1 million in available cap space , according to PuckPedia. Montreal will need to get creative in order to add more cap space to this roster. This could lead them to take the route of simply taking a flier. Korchinski, for example, is on a $1.3 million cap hit. Alexander Nikishin, another trade candidate, carries just a $3 million cap hit. Whitecloud makes even less than that. The Habs can create cap space if they need to. However, their most obvious cap-clearing candidates were traded in the Larkin deal. Kirby Dach and Samuel Montembeault were both included in the deal with the Red Wings. This leaves some key veterans, such as Phillip Danault and Josh Anderson, as potential cap casualties in any trade. The Canadiens would deal from a position of strength, so it wouldn’t hurt too much. However they make it happen, the Canadiens must add another defenseman before the 2027 NHL trade deadline. Doing so would make an already formidable team even more daunting come playoff time. Both the club and the Polish goalkeeper view the end of the season as a natural conclusion to his spell in Spain. Having barely featured on the pitch this term, the veteran is ready to step back after adding several trophies to his collection. This planned exit explains Barcelona’s surprising move to recruit Dominik Livakovic during the summer transfer window. Many questioned the €2 million signing at the time, given that Joan Garcia had already cemented the starting spot and the academy boasts promising third-choice options. However, the Catalan club brought in the 31-year-old specifically to succeed Szczesny. Inside Barcelona's long-term goalkeeping strategy Barcelona’s hierarchy structured the summer deal to give Livakovic a full season to adapt without immediate matchday pressure. Arriving a year early allows the Croatian international to learn his tactical responsibilities behind the scenes before taking on formal backup duties. Internally, sporting officials view the modest €2m fee as a low-risk investment that adds proven international pedigree to the dressing room. Livakovic arrived with minimal baggage and realistic expectations, having served as Croatia’s long-time starting goalkeeper. The club fully back him to step up reliably whenever called upon behind Garcia . Smart squad management at Camp Nou This proactive approach prevents a sudden summer scramble for an experienced deputy once Szczesny departs. Rather than rushing a youth prospect into high-stakes first-team cover, Barcelona have balanced academy depth with seasoned international reliability. For Szczesny, leaving in June allows him to bow out on a high note after fulfilling his short-term role in Catalonia. Meanwhile, Livakovic’s bargain transfer fee preserves financial discipline while securing stability behind Garcia for the foreseeable future. Copa del Rey offers Livakovic a chance to impress Livakovic has endured a quiet start in Spain, making just one appearance against Sevilla early in the campaign. Unless Garcia suffers an unforeseen injury, the Croatian will continue to see limited action in league fixtures. However, the upcoming start of the Copa del Rey offers a vital opportunity for Livakovic to build rhythm ahead of his promotion next summer. Szczesny, meanwhile, will see out the final months of his contract before closing the curtain on his Barcelona career in June.

title: Bayern-linked Mohya frustrated with Gladbach's "bitter draw" in Bremen as Schröder backs Blessin
summary: Borussia Mönchengladbach rued their missed opportunity to leave the Bundesliga basement as they conceded two late goals in a 3-3 draw with Werder Bremen. When Germany international Wael Mohya set up ...
content: Bayern-linked Mohya frustrated with Gladbach's "bitter draw" in Bremen as Schröder backs Blessin Borussia Mönchengladbach rued their missed opportunity to leave the Bundesliga basement as they conceded two late goals in a 3-3 draw with Werder Bremen. When Germany international Wael Mohya set up Franck Honorat's first Bundesliga brace, it felt like they'll register their second win of the season, but they failed to hold on to a two-goal. "The way we played, it's incredibly frustrating that we couldn't get the three points,” the 17-year-old Mohya said after the game. “There were lapses in concentration. We have to defend consistently and with focus for the entire 90 minutes." The attacking midfielder produced another strong performance as Gladbach played one of their best games to date. The sought-after youngster already has two goals and two assists to his name despite his club rooted to the bottom of the standings. Alexander Blessin agreed with the emerging star on the frustrating manner his side dropped points. “We punished ourselves and didn't reap the rewards.” Gladbach's coach said after the game. “It's bitter to put into words. We played an outstanding game and normally we should have left here as deserved winners. To get out of this situation, we'll have to win games like this.” The sporting director of the Foals Rouven Schröder supported his latest hire after the disappointing result as he called the 53-year-old "the right man in the right place". Blessin was unable to keep St. Pauli in the Bundesliga last term. Goalkeeper Daniel Batz revisited the moment that led to Niclas Füllkrug's injury-time equalizer after a lapse in concentration from the captain Philipp Sander. “I tried to get to the ball, but Füllkrug is flexible. He somehow managed to get his leg in there.” the 35-year-old told reporters after the final whistle.

title: Bayern Munich boss eager to move on from controversy surrounding Joshua Kimmich, Jamal Musiala

content: Former PSV player Marc Degryse believes Kevin De Bruyne should consider leaving Napoli during the January transfer window, arguing that the Belgian midfielder is not playing to his strengths under Massimiliano Allegri. De Bruyne has been linked with a move to PSV in recent weeks, with the Eindhoven club reportedly keen to bring him to the Eredivisie. PSV have already made an opening offer of €2 million , but Napoli rejected the proposal, leaving the potential transfer far from straightforward. Degryse discussed the midfielder's situation on VTM ahead of Napoli's Champions League meeting with Manchester City, which ended in a 2-2 draw. Noa Lang, another former PSV player, scored for the Italian side. The former Belgian international believes De Bruyne risks facing criticism if Napoli fail to challenge for major honours. "With this Napoli, De Bruyne won't win any prizes. And if that doesn't work out, he'll take all the criticism as the best player," Degryse said. Napoli Make Kevin De Bruyne Stance Clear Amid PSV Transfer Interest Sporting director Giovanni Manna quashed January exit rumors despite the Belgian playmaker’s struggles with Italian media and PSV’s persistent interest in bringing the veteran back to Benelux. De Bruyne Struggling to Find His Best Role at Napoli Degryse also pointed to the difference between De Bruyne's responsibilities at Napoli and the roles he enjoyed at Manchester City and with Belgium. The midfielder established himself as one of the world's leading playmakers during his time under Pep Guardiola at City, where his passing range, movement and ability to dictate attacking play made him central to the team's success. However, Degryse feels the Belgian is being used in a way that does not allow him to influence matches in the same manner. "If you compare it with his time at City or even with the Red Devils, that is always a completely different story from how he has to play at Napoli. He just doesn't come into his own there," the analyst concluded, as quoted by PSV Inside. A change of club could therefore offer De Bruyne the opportunity to return to a role more suited to his qualities. PSV are monitoring the situation, although Napoli's rejection of their first offer shows that negotiations would require further progress. Former Ajax midfielder Rafael van der Vaart has openly welcomed the prospect, describing the potential transfer as an exciting development for PSV. "That would be so much fun. If that happens, I'll be very happy," Van der Vaart said on Ziggo Sport's Rondo . He also highlighted De Bruyne's experience and quality, suggesting that even at this stage of his career, the Belgian could make a significant impact in the Eredivisie. Former PSV player Nordin Amrabat also sees the midfielder fitting into the team's attacking structure. He believes De Bruyne's creativity could complement players such as Guus Til and Ruben van Bommel . Guus Hiddink, however, has urged caution. While recognising the appeal of signing a player of De Bruyne's calibre, the former PSV coach warned that the financial demands of a deal must be considered. "There will be a price tag attached to it and PSV will have to think about that," Hiddink said. For now, De Bruyne's future remains uncertain. title: Hansi Flick’s Barcelona defensive record raises concerns despite convincing wins
summary: Barcelona’s 4-1 Champions League victory over Sabah offered a strong reminder of Hansi Flick’s defensive concerns, with the German coach visibly frustrated after his team conceded a late goal desp...
content: Hansi Flick’s Barcelona defensive record raises concerns despite convincing wins Barcelona’s 4-1 Champions League victory over Sabah offered a strong reminder of Hansi Flick’s defensive concerns, with the German coach visibly frustrated after his team conceded a late goal despite holding a comfortable 4-0 lead. As such, the reaction was not merely a disappointment at losing a clean sheet. Rather, Barcelona’s defensive consistency has become a recurring issue under Flick, and the goal in Azerbaijan could actually prove relevant when the Champions League league phase standings are decided. Although Barça have continued to score freely, their inability to regularly shut out opponents has left the team with a defensive record that contrasts sharply with their attacking output. Barcelona’s clean sheet record highlights a persistent problem Statistically, Barcelona have kept only five clean sheets in their first 18 matches of the 2026-27 season, which came against Aston Villa, Getafe, Valencia, Athletic Club and Elche. Notably, three of those five clean sheets came during the opening four La Liga matchdays. Since the fifth fixture against Feyenoord, the defence has shut out only Getafe and Aston Villa. Every other opponent has scored, including teams Barcelona eventually defeated by significant margins. The pattern clearly shows that Flick’s side has struggled to control games defensively even when their attacking quality has been enough to secure victories. Conceding against weaker opposition can prove costly in competitions where goal difference and points determine final positions. Flick’s Barcelona have conceded in two-thirds of his matches To put things in perspective, Barcelona have conceded in 90 of Flick’s 135 matches as head coach, meaning the team has failed to keep a clean sheet in exactly two-thirds of his games. Barcelona still need to work on keeping a clean sheet. (Picture credit: Barcelona website) The breakdown records 39 matches in which Barcelona conceded during the 2024-25 season and another 38 in 2025-26. That consistency across two campaigns indicates the issue has not been confined to a temporary dip in form. Barcelona’s defensive record is also reflected in the number of goals conceded. Flick’s team allowed 72 goals in his first season and 63 in his second. The 72-goal total was the club’s worst in at least 18 years, highlighting the contrast between their attacking success and defensive vulnerability. Indeed, Barcelona have generally avoided conceding excessively in individual matches, but their inability to regularly preserve a lead or finish games without allowing a goal is still a big concern.

content: Liverpool plotting January move for Ligue 1 star Liverpool Transfer News: Lamine Camara Interest Revived as January Window Nears Liverpool’s planning for the January market is beginning to come into sharper focus, with Give Me Sport reporting that Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara remains firmly on the club’s radar. The Merseyside club made three additions in the summer, bringing in Ronald Araujo, Victor Munoz and Bradley Barcola, and the early months of the campaign have offered encouragement. Liverpool have settled into the top four and, despite a few setbacks, there is a sense that further depth could push the side forward in the second half of the season. Midfield is understood to be one of the key areas under consideration. Camara has been monitored for some time, and there is now a growing feeling that circumstances may open a more realistic route for Liverpool to act when the market reopens. Lamine Camara back in Liverpool thinking Interest in the Senegal international did not disappear after the summer. Liverpool were attentive to his situation then, and when Chelsea attempted to move late in the window, they made their own contact clear. As reported, “And then just final word on Lamine Camara, like I said on deadline day exclusively, Liverpool were calling Camara on deadline day, and they were saying, ‘If you don’t go to Chelsea, we could be there for you in 2027,’” a detail that underlines how serious their admiration has been behind the scenes. Photo IMAGO That contact matters now because Chelsea’s failed pursuit appears to have changed the landscape. The same report adds, “And Liverpool privately, according to my information, were very glad that Camara and Chelsea fell through, and it seems like now Chelsea want Alex Scott.” For Liverpool, that potentially removes a major domestic rival from the immediate picture. It also suggests the club have remained alert to any shift in market conditions, rather than treating Camara as a passing target. Monaco stance could shape January move Any deal remains dependent on Monaco. Their refusal to complete business with Chelsea on deadline day has left tensions behind the scenes, and that could have consequences if the London club try to reopen talks. It was explained that, “Chelsea were really disappointed by Monaco’s handling there, which means if they are to renegotiate for Camara and move away from Alex Scott, they would likely need Monaco to make a significant concession, and that club-to-club relationship is still very difficult.” That leaves Liverpool in a healthier position if they choose to test the waters. There is no indication of an advanced negotiation yet, but the conditions look more favourable than they did a few months ago. Monaco’s domestic struggles could become another factor. Clubs under pressure rarely welcome losing major players in January, yet finances can alter the calculation quickly. If Liverpool decide Camara is a priority, they are one of the few sides capable of presenting an offer strong enough to force serious consideration. Why Camara appeals to Liverpool Camara’s profile makes obvious sense. He is energetic, technically secure and tactically mature, all traits that suit a side trying to compete across multiple fronts. The admiration from inside Monaco has also been striking. Filipe Luis said, “We are probably talking about one of the best midfielders in the world.” He added, “I don’t want to talk about him too much, because I know a lot of clubs would love to have him in their squad, and he is very important to me.” There was further praise too, with the Monaco boss saying, “He has that quality on the ball, covers a lot of ground, he is truly top class! I am really happy to have him, and he is going to play a key role in the team.” Those comments only reinforce why Liverpool have kept him in view. They point to a player trusted by his manager, valued by his club and admired by elite-level recruiters. Our View This is the sort of update that immediately gets the pulse racing. Liverpool clearly did more than admire Camara from afar, they made contact, stayed aware of the situation and were “very glad that Camara and Chelsea fell through”. That sounds like a club waiting for the right moment rather than walking away. Camara looks exactly the kind of midfielder Liverpool should be targeting, dynamic, smart, comfortable in possession and capable of covering ground at intensity. When a manager is saying, “We are probably talking about one of the best midfielders in the world,” supporters are always going to take notice. That may be glowing praise, but it matches the impression of a player with enormous upside. The most exciting part is the competitive angle. If Chelsea are moving towards Alex Scott and relations with Monaco remain strained, Liverpool could have a genuine opening. That does not mean it will be easy in January, because Monaco will fight to keep such an important player, but it puts Liverpool in a strong position if they decide to act decisively. If the recruitment team believe he can lift the level for the run-in, this feels like one worth pushing hard for. Camara has the profile, the talent and the ceiling to become a major piece of Liverpool’s midfield for years.

content: Liverpool remain keen on January move for midfielder Liverpool Transfer Latest: Lamine Camara Interest Could Open Up January Midfield Move Liverpool’s midfield planning is coming back into focus ahead of the January window, with Lamine Camara once again emerging as a name of genuine interest. According to Ben Jacobs for Give Me Sport , the Monaco midfielder remains on Liverpool’s radar after serious background work was carried out during the summer. There is a sense that Andoni Iraola wants to give his squad an extra layer for the second half of the campaign. Liverpool have made a solid start, helped by the arrivals of Ronald Araujo, Victor Munoz and Bradley Barcola, and the club’s recruitment team appear to be assessing whether another midfield addition can raise the level again. Lamine Camara Back in Liverpool Thinking Camara is not a new target. Liverpool tracked the Senegal international during the previous window and, when Chelsea attempted to land him late on, the Merseyside club made their own interest known. The latest update suggests that contact from Liverpool was more than routine due diligence. As reported by Give Me Sport, the position was made clear in direct terms: “And then just final word on Lamine Camara, like I said on deadline day exclusively, Liverpool were calling Camara on deadline day, and they were saying, ‘If you don’t go to Chelsea, we could be there for you in 2027,’” he said. That line is revealing. It points to a club thinking beyond one window and trying to establish trust early, a familiar feature of modern elite recruitment. Liverpool have often moved this way when they identify a player capable of fitting the sporting model and the financial framework. Chelsea Situation May Help Liverpool Another significant part of the update concerns Chelsea’s failed pursuit and the damage done to that route. Monaco’s refusal to complete the process in time appears to have changed the landscape, and Liverpool may now be in a stronger position if they choose to act. The same report states: “And Liverpool privately, according to my information, were very glad that Camara and Chelsea fell through, and it seems like now Chelsea want Alex Scott.” It adds that, “Unless they get a big concession on the deal, it might be difficult for Chelsea to go back to Monaco and sign Camara, because the club relationship is a bit broken because Monaco didn’t send that deal to a deal sheet.” Photo: IMAGO There is also further clarity on that breakdown: “Chelsea were really disappointed by Monaco’s handling there, which means if they are to renegotiate for Camara and move away from Alex Scott, they would likely need Monaco to make a significant concession, and that club-to-club relationship is still very difficult.” If that remains the case, Liverpool may have something close to a clear lane. Whether they choose to drive through it in January is the live question. Monaco Stance and January Challenge Monaco are not expected to make this easy.
